newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses slip, dlr rises after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses slip, dlr rises after U.S. data.

text.p: European stocks slid with Wall Street after data suggesting the strong U.S. economy was starting to show a pickup in inflation.
The dollar ended just off a 7-1/2 year high against the mark in Europe after monthly U.S. jobs figures and the National Association of Purchasing Management's (NAPM) July report.

U.S. July nonfarm payrolls jumped 316,000, pushing the unemployment rate down to 4.8 percent from 5.0 percent in June. A Reuters survey had predicted a 193,000-payrolls gain and a 4.9-percent jobless rate.

But average hourly earnings, used as an inflation gauge, remained flat at $12.23 per hour in July, while the average work week slipped to 34.4 hours from June's 34.7, indicating little threat of inflation from wages.
With few worries of wage-push inflation from the jobs report, U.S. bond prices managed to steady at lower levels and allow the Dow Jones Industrial Average to erase opening losses.
But gains were short-lived with the NAPM saying the manufacturing sector remained strong but amid higher price pressures than before.
NAPM's July index of manufacturing activity rose to 58.6 from June's 55.7 and forecasts for 56.1.

But traders were more concerned with NAPM's prices paid component, which rose to 53.6 to post its first move above 50 in four months. An index above 50 is often seen as a sign of expansion, while a figure below 50 is seen as a contraction.

"We had two warning signals today," said Robert Dederick, economic consultant at Northern Trust Co. "One in the employment report, which suggested that pressures in the labor market are there with no sign of abatement and another in this report, which shows that manufacturing is not devoid of capacity stress."

Dana Johnson, managing director and head of research at First Chicago, said "the question is whether the economic strength and labor market tightness that we're seeing is causing any wage and price pressures. There is a hint of that in the NAPM but really, only a hint of it."
Any signs of inflation amid a strong U.S. economy are likely to spark fears the Federal Reserve will have to raise interest rates at its next policy-making meeting on August 19.

U.S. bond prices extended losses and the Dow fell sharply after the NAPM report. The Dow was off 113.81 points at 8,108.80 at Europe's close and the benchmark 30-year U.S. bond yield was up near 6.43 percent from 6.30 percent at Thursday's U.S. close. Bond prices are inversely-related to bond yields.
Weakness in U.S. markets quickly rippled through Europe and sent government bonds and stock markets lower.
London's FTSE-100 and Paris' CAC-40 index quickly dropped to session lows but recovered some ground by the close.

FTSE losses were limited with help from a nine percent jump in Lloyds TSB Group Plc after the bank announced a higher-than-expected dividend of 5.3 pence, reported pre-tax earnings of 1.504 billion pounds ($2.5 billion) and said it would consider a share buyback if it failed to find a suitable acquisition.
FTSE losses were also tempered by mixed market views on whether the Bank of England would raise interest rates at its monthly meeting on Wednesday and Thursday.

"There is a strong two-way pull on opinion as to where UK interest rates are headed in the short term, though most agree that in the long term, rates are going up," Richard Jeffrey, strategist at brokerage Charterhouse Tilney, said.
In France, losses were capped by about a six-percent rise in Alcatel Alsthom after the firm said first-half sales rose 17 percent and several brokers upgraded the stock.
Alcatel closed up 6.18 percent at 859 francs ($138) but off its year high of 885 set earlier in the day.

German shares also slipped, with the IBIS DAX index shedding about 100 points, or more than two percent, in electronic trading. Investors sold stock before the weekend to lock in profits made in the recent rally to record peaks.
Daimler-Benz AG was among the weakest shares after two investment banks cut their earnings estimates for the company.

Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley downgraded Daimler's 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates despite the company's more than doubling of its operating profit in its six-month earnings report. Daimler shares ended down 5.90 marks at 148.90 but off its session low of 147.20.
Scandinavian bourses fared somewhat better, with Oslo's Total share index ending down 3.89 points, or 0.3 percent, at 1,284.78 from Thursday's record close.
Swedish shares also ended little changed, up 0.04 percent at 3,158.31.
Switzerland's bourse was closed for a holiday.
CURRENCIES AT THE CLOSE
The dollar was at 1.8630 marks and 118.37 yen from 1.8380 and 118.40 in late trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed down 8.2 points at 4,899.30.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index ended down 30.14 points in bourse trade at 4,408.79. The IBIS DAX lost 68.54 points at 4,336.98 in electronic trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 finished down 26.23 points at 3,049.44.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed in London at $324.25, down from Thursday's close at $324.90. ($ = 7.989 Swedish Crowns) ($ = 2.079 Dutch Guilders) ($ = 0.610 British Pounds) ($ = 6.224 French Francs)
